comments.why: Explains why LA's shade balls are black.
comments.text: [VIDEO] Veritasium video about Los Angeles' reservoir black spheres project. They used black because - The goal was light-blocking more than anything else; black worked best - The black pigment held up to the environment (especially UV degradation) better than anything else they tried I expect the second point was the most important thing. Black plastic is very stable.

comments.author: vanderZwan
comments.story: Mixing Is the Heartbeat of Deep Lakes. At Crater Lake, It's Slowing Down
comments.why: Shade balls as a cooling idea.
comments.text: I think that's the wrong way round: climate change causes longer summers and shorter winters, so the problem is one of cooling, not heating. Shade balls[0] could work, but then they'd have to cover part of the lake with that. EDIT: And of course, that also comes with a reduction in total light reaching the lake, which may have different side effects beyond temperature alone. [0] [VIDEO]

comments.author: thamer
comments.story: Largest Floating Solar Power Plant Taking Shape on Hydropower Plant
comments.why: Covers LA shade balls used to prevent evaporation.
comments.text: Shading is used in California to prevent evaporation, see for example the well-documented use of "shade balls": [LINK] Their use in Los Angeles was covered in a Veritasium video that was all over YouTube for a while (97M views): [VIDEO] The estimate given when they were added in 2015 – in the middle of a record drought – was that they would prevent the loss of 300 million gallons of water each year.
